title: An Efficient Diffusion-based Non-Autoregressive Solver for Traveling Salesman Problem

problem.claim: Solve Traveling Salesman Problems with neural models while avoiding substantial hand-crafted engineering.

gap.claim: Non-autoregressive approaches provide faster parallel inference but typically produce lower-quality solutions than autoregressive approaches.

contributions.claim: DEITSP is a diffusion-based non-autoregressive solver for TSP designed to improve solution quality while retaining fast inference.

The method combines one-step diffusion with controlled discrete noise, self-consistency enhancement, simultaneous denoising of multiple solutions, and a dual-modality graph transformer for node-edge feature extraction and fusion.
The method uses efficient alternating noise addition and removal together with progressive noise-level scheduling to refine the solution space and improve exploration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world and large-scale TSP instances reportedly show favorable performance against existing neural approaches in solution quality, inference latency, and generalization ability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural models show promise for solving TSP without much hand-crafted engineering.
NAR methods are faster through parallelism but generally have worse solution quality than autoregressive methods.
The paper proposes DEITSP, an efficient-iteration diffusion-based NAR TSP solver.
DEITSP combines one-step diffusion, self-consistent simultaneous denoising, dual-modality graph encoding, efficient iterative noise changes, and progressive noise scheduling.
Experiments on real-world and large-scale instances report favorable quality, latency, and generalization relative to existing neural approaches.

source_observation.claim: The paper addresses a quality-speed tradeoff by combining non-autoregressive parallelism with diffusion-based refinement and exploration.

interpretation.claim: Fast parallel inference can be paired with structured iterative refinement to mitigate quality loss.

application.claim: For parallel combinatorial solvers, consider combining multiple-solution prediction with controlled noise schedules and lightweight iterative refinement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy transfers beyond TSP or across all instance distributions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or statistical evaluation details.
The abstract does not describe computational costs, training procedures, or failure cases.
